articles.title: Rupee rises 7 paise to close at 93.44 against US dollar
articles.excerpt:
The rupee pared some of its initial gains and settled for the day higher by 7 paise at 93.44 (provisional) against the US dollar on Wednesday, as a decline in domestic equity markets and a strong greenback played spoilsport notwithstanding support from lower crude oil prices.

Forex traders said the rupee reversed its morning gains on risk aversion in global markets on fresh geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, and a strong dollar.

However, a sharp fall in crude oil prices supported the Indian currency.

articles.title: Rupee ends flat after hitting seven-month high as firmer dollar offsets inflows
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee closed almost flat after peaking at a seven-month high during early trading on Wednesday. Robust foreign investments in local stocks provided a boost, but a stronger dollar capped further gains. The dollar index rose by 0.2%, reaching its highest since April 2025 due to anticipations of accelerated rate hikes.

articles.title: Rupee appreciates for third consecutive day as oil dips
articles.excerpt:
The rupee appreciated for the third consecutive day, opening at ₹93.30 per US dollar as crude oil prices continued to fall and market sentiment improved.

The local currency rose 18 paise at open on November 18, marking its third consecutive session of gains. It was trading at around ₹93.40 a dollar during the first few hours of the session. Rupee has appreciated by over 90 paise in the last three sessions. It last saw these levels on April 17, 2026, when it was at ₹92.60.

Crude oil prices fall as US inventory build outweighs West Asia tensions

The increase is attributed to lower crude prices and renewed FPI interest in Indian stocks.

Anil Bhansali, Head of Treasury at Finrex Treasury Adv

articles.title: Gold recovers from one-year low as markets assess Fed rate outlook
articles.excerpt:
Gold prices climbed 0.6%, rebounding from a recent slide to a 14-month low, amidst persistent investor anxiety. With the US Federal Reserve's scrutiny over interest rates intensified to curb inflation, experts foresee a 90% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December. Concurrently, the Bank of Japan is gearing up for its third rate hike this year, which has catalyzed positive movement in precious metals like silver and platinum.

articles.title: Gold Slumps 3% to Lowest in Over a Year on Hawkish Fed Signals
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold tumbled over 3% to the lowest in over a year after Federal Reserve officials made the case for more interest-rate hikes to tackle stubborn inflation.

Bullion fell as much as 3.1% on a third day of declines after Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said inflation remains headed in the wrong direction, urging the central bank to consider a larger, half-percentage-point rate hike at its December meeting.

“We have to be a little more aggressive in our rate hikes to try to get inflation down,” Waller said Wednesday on CNBC.
